decisive_items: on day 33 of an organized hunger strike
BMI had reduced from 22.9 kg/m² to 19.4 kg/m²
response.rationale: The prolonged hunger strike and significant weight loss, combined with bloody diarrhea and colitis findings, directly support starvation-induced colitis. R2 and R3 are similar but less precise, while R8 and R4 are broader and lack the specific etiologic link.

rejected.why: Clostridium difficile toxin was not present, directly contradicting this diagnosis.
Same as R1; toxin absence rules out C. difficile infection.
Ulcerative colitis is a specific IBD subtype but the hunger strike context is the key etiologic factor, not clearly supported.
Inflammatory bowel disease is too broad and does not capture the starvation-induced mechanism.
Ischemic colitis is not supported by the imaging or biopsy findings; abdominal tenderness alone is insufficient.
Similar to R2 but less directly tied to the colitis mechanism; R5 is more precise.
